Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates dextrocardia, evidenced by the cardiac silhouette and apex pointing to the right side of the patient's chest. Kartagener's syndrome is characterized by the triad of situs inversus (which includes a right-sided heart), chronic sinusitis, and bronchiectasis; therefore, the finding of a right-sided heart (implying a left-sided liver in situs inversus totalis) supports this diagnosis.
